title: QODIQA Webhook Protocol Conformance Vectors
description: Schema for test-vectors/webhook-v1.json. Every SDK implementation (present and future) consumes vectors matching this schema without any language-specific transformation of the file itself. See test-vectors/README.md for the full contract.

protocolVersion.description: Webhook signature protocol version these vectors describe. Bump this (and the filename, e.g. webhook-v2.json) if the wire protocol ever intentionally changes.

id.description: Unique, stable, kebab-case identifier. Do not reuse or repurpose an id once published — add a new vector instead.

scenario.description: The genuine, self-consistent inputs a real server delivery would have used. Server-side conformance tests use ONLY this object: recompute computeSignature(secret, timestamp, body) and assert it equals expectedSignature.

timestamp.description: Raw X-QODIQA-Timestamp value the server would have sent, ISO-8601 UTC.

body.description: Raw UTF-8 request body exactly as the server would have sent it.

expectedSignature.description: sha256=<hex>, produced by calling the real production computeSignature(). Never hand-written.

verify.description: What is actually handed to an SDK's verifier. For positive vectors this is identical to `scenario` (with secrets=[scenario.secret]). For negative vectors, one or more fields are deliberately altered from `scenario` to exercise a specific failure mode.

body.description: Body to pass as the SDK verifier's `body` argument.

signature.description: Raw X-QODIQA-Signature header value to pass to the verifier. May be malformed, empty, or a comma-joined duplicate-header simulation in negative vectors.

timestamp.description: Raw X-QODIQA-Timestamp header value to pass to the verifier. May be malformed, empty, or a comma-joined duplicate-header simulation in negative vectors.

secrets.description: Secret(s) the SDK is configured with when calling verify(). Pass as-is to the SDK's `secret` parameter (single value or list, per that SDK's API).

verifyAt.description: The wall-clock instant (ISO-8601 UTC) at which verification is deemed to occur. Pass this to the SDK's test-only 'override current time' hook (Python: _now as epoch seconds; JS: _now as epoch seconds) so replay-tolerance vectors are deterministic regardless of when the suite actually runs. Convert to epoch seconds if your SDK's override expects that.

tolerance.description: Replay-tolerance window in seconds to configure the verifier with for this vector.

expectedError.description: Canonical error category the verifier must raise when expectedResult is 'invalid'; null when expectedResult is 'valid'. Every SDK must map its own exception/error class names onto these four canonical categories.
